14:72.targetText: Тогда петух запел во второй раз. И вспомнил Петр слово, сказанное ему Иисусом: прежде нежели петух пропоет дважды, трижды отречешься от Меня; и начал плакать.

groups.note: Actual finite active saying with Jesus as subject becomes Russian passive attributive with Jesus as agent and the same words as what was said.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual initial additive is implicit.
Actual immediacy is unexpressed. Russian gives its time transition instead.
Actual preposition belongs to the temporal ordinal idiom. Russian marks the second occurrence with its own ordinal phrase.
Actual manner conjunction introduces how Jesus said the words. Russian gives the passive attributive.
Actual speech marker is expressed by punctuation.
Actual separate preceding participle ἐπιβαλὼν is idiomatic in this setting. Russian expresses the onset of weeping without rendering a separate act.
These printed Greek articles are unexpressed in the local Russian noun, modifier or infinitive phrases.

Russian uses this preposition in its temporal ordinal phrase. Actual Greek has a differently marked ἐκ idiom.
Russian makes the occurrence explicit with a noun. Actual Greek uses the ordinal phrase without an occurrence noun.
Actual person denied is bare accusative. Russian makes this a prepositional complement.
